reasons: Both answers meet every rubric item with nearly identical warnings, workarounds, test-print advice and mini-appropriate Cura settings. A covers the full range of workarounds, including a smaller nozzle and its time cost given the deadline, and adds Cura's thin-feature controls (minimum feature size) and Z-hop to protect thin parts. B adds useful points (Arachne, the scale-up calculation, timing estimate, license) but omits the nozzle-swap option and includes an odd phrase ('under our usual quality bar'), so A edges it slightly.
